description: The ground-floor lobby of The Meridian, a residential tower that survived the Collapse the same way most things survived it: through sheer institutional inertia. Cracked terrazzo floors carry the ghost of a geometric inlay, ground to near-invisibility by foot traffic. A bank of tenant mailboxes lines the east wall, most of them pried open decades ago, doors hanging at odd angles, contents long gone. The security desk sits unmanned, its terminal cycling a screensaver of rolling static. Emergency lighting casts everything in pale amber. Stairs ascend through a fire door to the upper floors.

window.description: A full-height pane onto the street, kept just clean enough to trade through. Whatever the weather is doing out there, it is doing it in plain view.
window.name: the shopfront window
